issues.body: The validator still performs the prohibited-key lookup only under `if isinstance(flow, dict) and "leases" in flow`. A parseable snapshot such as `{"schema":"registry-observability/v1","flow":[{"leases":[{"label":"ab12cd340a5f9e71"}]}]}` therefore returns no violations even though the public bytes contain the refused per-account array. The `alien` self-test instead makes the entire document a list, which is rejected by the earlier top-level-object check and does not exercise this bypass. This is materially the same defect recorded in round 4.
issues.fix_hint: When `flow` is present, fail closed unless its value is an object; preserve acceptance of an absent `flow` only if that is intentional. Add a literal fixture with an object top level and a non-object `flow` containing nested `leases`, assert the specifically classified `validate()` refusal, and include it in the real CLI exit-code table with expected code 1.
issues.title: Non-object flow still bypasses the public-byte lease-row invariant

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 bypass remains unchanged. `_snapshot_violations` rejects a non-object top-level document, but a valid top-level object whose present `flow` value is a list, string, null, or other non-object still returns no violations. The self-test again covers only a non-object top-level document, so it does not exercise the reported seam. Because the same major finding remains at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
